caption:
Think Pilates is just stretching? Lulu did too, until the first session on the reformer.

Clinical Pilates is resistance training on springs. The springs load muscles as they lengthen and shorten, and the slow, controlled pace is often tougher than it looks. It can also cover what heavy lifting skips: rotation, single-leg control and strength at end range.

It's a practical option when a back, hip or shoulder niggle makes the gym awkward, because load can be adjusted spring by spring. And you don't need to touch your toes to start.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with an assessment and builds a program around your goals. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
